title: Reorder List
statement:
You are given the head of a singly linked list. Reorder the list to be on the following form: `L0 -> Ln -> L1 -> Ln-1 -> L2 -> Ln-2 -> ...`

You may not modify the values in the list's nodes; only nodes themselves may be changed.

Build the list from `values`, then: find the middle with slow/fast pointers, reverse the second half, and merge the two halves by alternating nodes. Convert the reordered chain back to an array.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [1, 5 * 10^4]

editorial.approach: First find the middle of the list using slow/fast pointers. Split the list into two halves and reverse the second half (standard three-pointer reversal). Then merge the two halves by alternately taking one node from the first half and one from the reversed second half, relinking `.next` pointers as you go. This achieves the L0, Ln, L1, Ln-1, ... pattern without extra space beyond a few pointers.
